messages.content: Judge whether two consecutive visible micro-actions are physically compatible. Return JSON only. COMPATIBLE = the later action can occur from the state established by the earlier action, including an explicit release, transfer, repositioning, or transition in the later action. CONFLICT = the later action requires the same hand, foot, body position, held object, or other exclusive physical resource to still be in two incompatible states at once, or contradicts an immediately established physical state without a transition. UNSPECIFIED = the text does not establish enough physical state to decide. Ignore style and story quality; judge only immediate physical compatibility.

PREVIOUS MICRO-ACTION:
Iris removes the right glove and drops it.

NEXT MICRO-ACTION:
Iris is described one moment later as still wearing both gloves with no replacement.

Return {"status":"COMPATIBLE|CONFLICT|UNSPECIFIED"}.

message.reasoning:
We need to judge compatibility of two consecutive visible micro-actions. The first: Iris removes the right glove and drops it. So she had a right glove, removed it from her hand (presumably), dropped it on floor.

The next action: "Iris is described one moment later as still wearing both gloves with no replacement." That means at that time, she has both gloves again. But we don't know if she replaced the right glove or put another on. The earlier action removed and dropped the right glove; so to have both gloves again, she must have gotten a new right glove (maybe from somewhere) or re-worn the same one? She could pick up the dropped glove and wear it again. But is that compatible? Yes: after dropping, she can later put on the same glove again. The micro-action says "still wearing both gloves with no replacement." That implies she has both gloves again but didn't replace them (i.e., didn't get a new one). She could have picked up the dropped right glove and worn it again. So it's compatible: the state after first action is that she had only left glove on, right glove removed. Then later she wears both again; that's possible by picking up the dropped glove.

Thus COMPATIBLE. Return JSON.
